# Unit Economics

This document exists because the price we intend to charge does not work, and the gap has a specific size.

## The result

| Metric | Value | Requirement | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| LTV/CAC at list price (Rs 120,000) | 0.21 | >= 3.0 | **FAIL by ~14x** |
| ACV required for LTV/CAC >= 3 | Rs 1,027,962 | - | **8.6x the list price** |
| Required ACV as share of NIT annual budget | 0.054% | affordable if < 1% | **PASS** |
| CAC (median) | Rs 719,276 | - | - |
| P(ARR >= Rs 1 crore by year 3) | 0.0% | hand estimate was 18-34% | **hand estimate falsified** |

## The shape of the problem

Two facts pull in opposite directions and both are true:

1. **The list price destroys the economics.** LTV/CAC of 0.21 means we lose roughly Rs 568,078 for every institution we acquire.
2. **The price that fixes it is affordable.** Rs 1,027,962 is about 0.054% of a NIT's annual budget, and about 0.05% of the unspent capacity each NIT carries. The budget does not object.

The conclusion follows directly and it is not comfortable: **the objection is willingness, not affordability.** Rs 53 crore of unspent capacity per NIT demonstrates that budgets go unspent. It does not demonstrate that anyone will spend it on us.

## Why the 18-34% estimate was wrong

The hand estimate double-counted conversion - it applied a conversion rate to an already-filtered population. Corrected, the seeded simulation returns a 0.0% probability of reaching Rs 1 crore ARR by year 3, with a P95 of roughly Rs 41 lakh.

That correction was made in Phase 3B and it is retained here rather than quietly dropped, because a model that only publishes its favourable numbers is not a model.

## The two scenarios, stated as a price question

| | Scenario A | Scenario B |
|---|---|---|
| ACV | Rs 120,000 | Rs 1,027,962 |
| Basis | our list price | what the model requires |
| LTV/CAC | 0.21 | 3.00 |
| Viable | no | on paper |
| Price evidence | none | none |

> **OQ-03 has been open since Phase 0.** This is the price the SALES MODEL demands, not the price the market bears. Budget evidence is not willingness evidence: the required ACV is ~0.054% of a NIT's annual budget, so affordability is not the objection. Nobody has agreed to pay it.

## What would settle it

Twelve interviews (6 institutions x 2 roles, Phase 3B). One question resolves most of it: what would it take for you to approve this budget line, and who else would need to agree?
